claims.text: The as-deposited CrMnFeCoNi HEA bond coat has a coarse-grained structure.
The as-deposited CrMnFeCoNi HEA bond coat contains inherent porosity.
The as-deposited CrMnFeCoNi HEA bond coat contains microcracks.
Controlled post-deposition thermomechanical annealing will promote recrystallization in the CrMnFeCoNi bond coat.
Controlled post-deposition thermomechanical annealing will refine the bond-coat grains to an ultrafine scale.
The treatment will reduce bond-coat porosity.
The treatment will reduce the number of microcracks in the bond coat.
Grain refinement will reduce stress-concentration sites.
The refined grain structure will provide enhanced diffusion paths.
Enhanced diffusion paths will facilitate formation of protective oxides.
Reduced stress concentrations and protective-oxide formation will mitigate oxidation during thermal cycling.
Reduced stress concentrations and protective-oxide formation will mitigate spallation during thermal cycling.
Compared with the untreated baseline, the annealed bond coat will have improved high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Compared with the untreated baseline, the annealed bond coat will have a lower spallation rate during cyclic thermal exposure.
Compared with the untreated baseline, the annealed bond coat will have enhanced mechanical durability.
The treatment should remain effective in cyclic oxidation environments at temperatures up to approximately 1100°C when its parameters are properly optimized.
Annealing at approximately 900°C for 1–2 hours in an inert or controlled atmosphere is the proposed treatment window.
Managed cooling will prevent grain coarsening and maintain beneficial residual stresses.
